module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 905

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/905](https://www.erdosproblems.com/905)
- [KhNi79] Khadzhiivanov, N. G. and Nikiforov, S. V., *Solution of a problem of P. Erdős about the
  maximum number of triangles with a common edge in a graph*. C. R. Acad. Bulgare Sci. (1979),
  1315-1318.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos905

open Finset

/--
Every graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges contains an edge which is in at least $n/6$
triangles.

A conjecture of Bollobás and Erdős. This was proved independently by Edwards (unpublished) and
Khadzhiivanov and Nikiforov [KhNi79].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos905.lean"]
theorem erdos_905 (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (#G.edgeFinset : ℝ)) :
    ∃ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, (n : ℝ) / 6 ≤ (#(G.trianglesContaining e) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos905

review.notes:
No misformalization found in the file's only declaration, Erdos905.erdos_905. The hypothesis `(n:ℝ)^2/4 < #G.edgeFinset` is "more than n²/4 edges". The conclusion `∃ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, n/6 ≤ #(G.trianglesContaining e)` is a conjunction, not an implication, and is "some edge lies in at least n/6 triangles". This matches erdosproblems.com/905 word for word.

Lean checks, all in /workspace/review:
(1) `trianglesContaining` equals the version using the ambient instances (`congr!`).
(2) For an edge uv, #(G.trianglesContaining s(u,v)) = #(common neighbours of u and v). Hence the conclusion is equivalent to "∃ u v, G.Adj u v ∧ n/6 ≤ #common neighbours" (`erdos_905_iff`).
(3) Concrete decide checks: K3 edges lie in 1 triangle. In K4 minus an edge, the counts are 2, 1, and 0 for the non-edge. The diagonal s(0,0) is not in edgeFinset.
(4) Brute-force #eval of the file's exact expressions over all graphs on up to 6 vertices. The hypothesis held for 1, 7, 176 and 4944 graphs at n = 3, 4, 5, 6 (the expected binomial counts), with 0 counterexamples. The minimum largest-book size was 1, 2, 2, 2, consistent with the strict bound bk > n/6.
(5) The hypothesis cannot be met for n ≤ 2, so the statement is vacuous there, which is harmless.

Literature: Bollobás–Nikiforov phrase the result as β(n, ⌊n²/4⌋+1) ≥ n/6 (once also 'at least ⌊n/6⌋') and prove bk(G) > n/6. Exactly ⌊n²/4⌋+1 edges and more than n²/4 edges give the same statement because the largest book cannot shrink when edges are added. The file's real-valued n/6 is the stronger form, is true, and follows the cited source.

Status is consistent: `research solved` plus `formal_proof using lean4`, and erdosproblems.com says 'PROVED (LEAN)'. The linked plby proof's headline theorem uses natural-number division in the conclusion (`Fintype.card V / 6 ≤ triangleDegree G e`, i.e. ⌊n/6⌋), which is weaker than the file's real n/6. The same proof file also proves `card_lt_six_mul_maxTriangleDegree_of_quarter_sq_lt_edges` (n < 6·β) and that some edge attains the maximum. I checked in Lean (`fc_of_key`) that this key lemma implies the file's exact statement, so the formal_proof record covers it. The linked file targets Lean v4.29.1 and does not compile unchanged on this repo's v4.33.1 toolchain (Mathlib API drift), which is expected.

Bibliographic aside, outside the mathematics: the module docstring lists '[KhNi79] Khadzhiivanov, N. G. and Nikiforov, S. V.'. Nikiforov's own bibliography (Bollobás–Nikiforov) has 'V. Nikiforov', and this repo's 1010.lean has 'Nikiforov, V. S.', so the initials look swapped. The references appear to be copied from erdosproblems.com's bibliography, which I could not fetch (Cloudflare, not archived), so I did not report it as a finding.
